input:
A gravity settler removes activated sludge from a process stream. The design overflow rate is 0.94 m h⁻¹ at a throughput of 139 m³ h⁻¹, giving a plan area of 148 m². The overflow rate is the throughput divided by the plan area, and the area follows from the rate the design adopts: a solid that settles at the overflow rate is removed, and a solid that settles more slowly leaves with the clarified stream. The sizing therefore rests on the overflow rate, and the overflow rate rests on the settling behaviour of the sludge.

The settler separates by density difference under gravity, with the feed introduced so that the upward velocity of the liquid stays below the settling velocity of the flocs to be removed. Residence time, inlet distribution and sludge withdrawal all bear on performance, but none enters the area figure, which the overflow-rate method fixes from the throughput alone.

The basis used here is a vendor rule for this solid. No settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the rate has not been checked against the material the settler will treat; a slurry whose flocs settle more slowly than the vendor rule assumes would need a larger area at the same throughput, and the stated area holds only as long as the vendor rule describes the actual sludge.
